newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKER AFTER CENTRAL BANK BUYING.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKER AFTER CENTRAL BANK BUYING.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar opened weaker against the key U.S. dollar on Friday in the aftermath of heavy foreign currency buying by the central bank late Thursday, dealers said.
"It looks like everyone is still a bit short after the Reserve Bank came into the market quite heavily yesterday," one dealer commented.
The central bank has been tightly monitoring the local currency, to keep it at levels compatible with inflation which rose to 22.4 percent in the year to April from 19.9 percent.
At around 0805 GMT on Friday, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.3125/3225 against the U.S. dollar from 11.3075/3175 on Thursday.

Against the crosses, it was quoted at 18.4515/4950 versus sterling from 18.4400/4600 the previous day, tracking a softer U.S. dollar overseas but strengthened slightly on the mark to 6.5220/5430 from 6.5400/5600. It was at 2.5220/5280 against the rand from 2.5200/5400.
